description: Shared Renovate preset for consumer orgs. Extend from a repo's renovate.json with: { "extends": ["github>jr200-labs/github-action-templates"] }

packageRules.description: Group every non-major bump into a single PR per repo. Schedule deliberately omitted so the wave lands immediately; grouping prevents PR-spam without needing a time window. No automerge — humans review every PR.
Ignore boto3 patch releases because they are published near-daily; minor releases provide a lower-noise update cadence.

Force fix(deps) for non-major Renovate commits so release-please consumers actually cut a patch release on merge. The :semanticCommits preset emits chore(deps) by default, which release-please's standard config treats as no-op — every Renovate merge would land but no version tag would follow, blocking downstream Renovate-driven rollouts (JRL-37).
Packages published by this organization are part of the same release pipeline, so they should roll forward immediately instead of waiting behind Renovate's release-age hold.
Major upgrades always require explicit human review. feat(deps) so release-please cuts a minor bump on merge (or major, depending on the consumer's release-please config).

Widen (don't bump) peer-dependency ranges on @opentelemetry/* so consumers stay free to upgrade without lib churn. The @opentelemetry/api package is a pluggable singleton contract — if a library pins a narrow peer range and a consumer has a different copy resolved alongside, provider.register() touches one copy while trace.getTracer() reads the other, resulting in silent no-op spans. Widening keeps the existing range satisfied while also admitting the new version.
Group all GitHub Action version bumps together
Group all Docker base image bumps together

Don't bump the Python runtime constraint — that's a deliberate stack decision and not something Renovate should touch. Also sidesteps the 'pep440: failed to calculate newValue' warning Renovate hits when trying to bump '>=3.12,<3.14' style ranges. review-by: 2026-10-09

Don't bump @duckdb/duckdb-wasm** on the pre-release `-devN.0` channel. Dev45 (2026-04-13) rewrote the HTTPWasmClient fetch path (commit 0c09da6) and broke module instantiation at load time with 'Body is disturbed or locked' — the Response body is consumed twice. Last known-good is 1.33.1-dev42.0. Recheck once duckdb-wasm cuts stable 1.33.1 (or later) with the HTTP refactor fixed. review-by: 2026-10-09

Don't bump @luma.gl/** or @deck.gl/** — @luma.gl/core is pinned at 9.2.6 with an SSR null-safety patch (patches/@luma.gl__core@9.2.6.patch). Bumping deck.gl to 9.3+ peer-requires @luma.gl/core ~9.3.2, which drops the patch via pnpm hoisting. Bumping @luma.gl/webgl alone causes Turbopack build failures (missing Fence export — only in core@9.3.0+). Keep the whole stack on 9.2.x until the patch is upstreamed or Next/Turbopack no longer trips on it. review-by: 2026-10-09

Disable Renovate's built-in helm-values manager first, then selectively re-enable it below. The custom regex managers own semver GHCR image pins under `services/.../env/.../*values.yaml`; running both managers for those pins produces duplicate, conflicting bump attempts.

Track non-GHCR images in Helm values with Renovate's built-in manager. The custom GHCR regex managers do not cover Docker Hub, registry.k8s.io, GCR, or other registries; leaving the blanket disable in effect silently hid their updates.

Track GHCR images outside the service values tree with Renovate's built-in manager. The custom GHCR regex managers are scoped to service manifests, so suppressing helm-values elsewhere leaves dependencies such as Ansible role values untracked.
Group shared workflow ref bumps. The reusable Renovate workflow repairs generated consumer files after Renovate creates or updates the branch.

Private git Python dependencies use repository package names, while uv's --upgrade-package expects Python distribution names. Keep dependencies published by this organization out of mixed PyPI groups and skip Renovate's automatic artifact updater; the shared uv lock postUpgradeTask below regenerates uv.lock with plain `uv lock`. Consumers from other organizations can add their namespaces in their repository-owned Renovate config.
Regenerate uv.lock with fresh package metadata whenever Renovate's pep621 manager changes Python dependencies in pyproject.toml.
Regenerate uv.lock when a Python-specific custom regex manager changes a dependency.

customManagers.description: Bump shared workflow/config refs pinned in consumer `.github/.shared-config.yaml` files. Refs use github-action-templates tags named `shared-vX.Y.Z` so drift repairs land as dedicated Renovate PRs instead of piggybacking onto unrelated feature work.
Bump private git-pinned Python deps in pep621 pyproject.toml — e.g. '<pkg>[extras] @ git+https://github.com/<org>/<pkg>.git@v0.7.3'

Refresh uv.lock digests for Python dependencies pinned to a GitHub master/main branch. The git-refs datasource detects branch-head changes; the shared uv post-upgrade task then refreshes package metadata in the same PR.

Bump container image tags in IaC Helm values.yaml — `tag: vX.Y.Z` under `repository: ghcr.io/<namespace>/<image>`. Query GHCR directly so releases are derived from published image tags instead of assuming a source repository has matching Git tags.

Bump inline `image: ghcr.io/<namespace>/<image>:vX.Y.Z` refs in IaC service manifests — Helm values.yaml and raw Kustomize manifests (statefulset/deployment/daemonset/cronjob/job/pod). Query the registry directly so the lookup follows published image tags.

Bump versions pinned via Dockerfile `ARG <FOO>_VERSION=...` lines preceded by a `# renovate: datasource=<ds> depName=<name>` annotation on the line immediately above. Each annotated ARG produces exactly one tracked dep, scoped to its own line. Replaces the prior matchStringsStrategy=combination approach which paired ARGs and ghcr.io references by file position, mis-attributing currentValues across unrelated tools (JRL-36).
